narrative:
This silver drachm originates from Maroneia in Thrace, dating to approximately 365-330 BC during the Classical Period. The coin's obverse features the legend ΜΑ(ΡΩ) alongside a depiction of a bunch of grapes on a vine branch within an incuse square border, surrounded by the name of the magistrate. The reverse displays the legend ΕΠΙ ΖΗΝΩΝΟΣ.

The coin's weight is 2.44 g with a diameter of 17 mm, and was likely produced under the authority of Magistrate Zenon. Scholarly sources, including Schonert-Geiss and Psoma et al., identify this coin as part of a reduced attic standard drachm.

Given the classification confidence of 83.5%, a verification of this identification is recommended. The coin's significance lies in its association with the mint of Maroneia and the historical context of the magistrate Zenon.
